subject: Deployment path: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — migration follow-up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@finsecure.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment path: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — migration follow-up

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap of what you shared:
- Current setup: in-house inference stack running a custom API wrapper on a 4x A100 cluster.
- Primary drivers: predictable latency for customers, cost visibility, and strict data residency/compliance for regulated customers.
- Shortlist: leaning toward Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput, but Private VPC/on-prem is on the table for regulated lines of business.
- Migration concern: minimize downtime and keep the current model serving contracts intact during cutover.

Open clarification questions (helps us size the right path):
1) Expected steady-state QPS and peak concurrent sessions (approx)?
2) Typical sequence lengths / model families you plan to run (Llama-derivative, LLM-XX, etc.)?
3) Any hard requirements on where keys / logs must live (specific cloud region, on-prem-only)?
4) Do you need SOC2/HIPAA evidence up front for procurement or will an attestation suffice for the POC?

Suggested immediate next steps:
- I attached a simple TCO calculator (redwood-tco-calculator.xlsx) to compare Hosted / Dedicated / Private for your current cluster — we can walk this together.
- Priyom (cc) can sketch an architecture for a Dedicated migration and what a Private VPC cutover would look like (routing, network, certs).
- If it helps, we can run a short POC migrating one model and serving behind your existing gateway to validate latency and throughput (2–3 week window).

Proposed times for a 30–45 min follow-up: Thu 3/18 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 3/19 8:00–9:00 PT. Does either work?

Thanks — I’ll hold the slots.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

[Attachment: redwood-tco-calculator.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Lena Park <lena.park@finsecure.io>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finsecure.io>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment path: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — migration follow-up

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers to your questions so you can start sizing: 
- Steady-state: ~80 qps on average, peaks to ~250 qps during batch job windows.
- Models: primarily a Llama-derivative (13B) plus a few 7B models for embeddings/rerank. Typical sequence lengths average 512–1,024 tokens.
- Data residency: production customer data must remain within us-west-2 for now. Logs can be archived to a different region but access controls are required.
- Compliance: Procurement needs SOC2 Type II evidence before program kickoff; for POC an attestation and a short statement of controls would be acceptable.

On preferences: for predictable SLAs we like the Dedicated approach — predictable throughput and easier cost forecasting. However, three of our regulated customers have contractual requirements that may force us to use a Private VPC for their traffic. So we need a path that lets us start on Dedicated and offer Private VPC for a subset of customers later. Migration-wise, zero-ish downtime is preferred — wrapping the new endpoint behind our existing gateway during cutover is the plan.

Can you send a commercial ballpark for both Dedicated and Private (monthly), and an outline of what the POC would include (scope, timeline, success criteria)? Procurement would like an initial estimate by EOD Monday to align budgets.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Head of ML Platforms | FinSecure, Inc.
lena.park@finsecure.io

[Procurement included on cc for budget timeline]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@finsecure.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment path: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — migration follow-up

Lena — perfect, thanks for the detail. Attached is the TCO calculator populated with a first-pass using your numbers and a one-page security checklist that maps to SOC2 artifacts we can share quickly. Highlights from the calc: 
- Hosted API (managed): fastest path to production but less deterministic per-tenant latency at peak; useful for early feature tests.
- Dedicated: ~25–30% lower unit cost for high sustained QPS compared to Hosted billing; gives predictable throughput and a clean isolation boundary.
- Private VPC: higher setup + monthly infra fee but satisfies strict residency/compliance; recommended for regulated customers where contractually required.

Proposed POC scope:
- Migrate one production model to a Dedicated pool (same instance types you currently use) and route a small % of traffic through it. Measure latency, p95/p99, and cost per 1M tokens. ~2 weeks.
- If you need, we can run a side-by-side Private VPC proof where we spin up a minimal VPC deploy for the same model to validate network and audit requirements (adds ~1 week).

Success criteria: p95 latency within 20% of current baseline, throughput that matches workload targets, and documented steps for cutover with rollback.

I asked Priyom to draft an architecture note (network, KV cache considerations, model quant/weights transport) and Aditya will prepare a ballpark commercial for Dedicated vs Private for you to share with Procurement.

I can hold Thu 3/18 10:00 PT for the POC kickoff call — confirm and I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda.

Thanks,
Camila

[Attachments: redwood-tco-calculator.xlsx (updated), redwood-security-checklist.pdf]
